words.gram: masculine accusative singular inanimate demonstrative pronoun

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?
You are under my roof now.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'at night' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We must forget that night.

examples.text: Я вам ночью уже всё сказал.
examples.trans: I already told you everything last night.
Good night!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.

examples.text: Тебя вспомнишь — и уже не так плохо.
examples.trans: One remembers you, and things do not seem so bad.
Well, there you go, it has started already.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У неё на новом месте всё в порядке.
examples.trans: Everything is fine with her at the new place.
Chef, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'said', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

examples.text: Ты сказал, что не будешь работать.
examples.trans: You said you would not work for me.

examples.text: Я вам ночью уже всё сказал.
examples.trans: I already told you everything last night.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And did you ever think of me?
There were difficult moments in life.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: Ты должен будешь исчезнуть из отеля.
examples.trans: You will have to disappear from the hotel.
We must forget that night.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'бавиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get rid of', paired with 'избавляться'.

related.gloss: to to get rid of (prefixed perfective)
not to to get rid of (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Ты должен избавиться от одного повара.
examples.trans: You must get rid of one cook.

examples.text: Ты хотел избавиться от моей жены?
examples.trans: Did you want to get rid of my wife.

examples.text: Нам нужно срочно избавиться от этого старого дивана.
examples.trans: We urgently need to get rid of this old sofa.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I work right here for you.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.
And did you ever think of me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'alone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Get out of my office!

examples.text: Ну я же не вчера родился, а?
examples.trans: Well, I was not born yesterday, huh?

examples.text: А что тут у вас происходит?
examples.trans: And what is going on here with you?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cook' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I work as a cook in the kitchen.

examples.text: Но он больше музыкант, чем повар.
examples.trans: But he is more of a musician than a cook.
Our head cook there got sick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: The chef built this wonderful restaurant.
Do it by any means necessary.

examples.text: Как ты вообще мог это сделать?
examples.trans: How could you do that at all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.trans: I love you. Do not miss me too much.
Do it by any means necessary.

examples.text: Можешь в любое время останавливаться в люксе.
examples.trans: You can stay in the luxury suite at any time.

meanings.en: way, method, means of doing something
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пособ'). Common masculine noun meaning 'by means / way' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do it by any means necessary.

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.
examples.trans: The strong man looks for a way, and the weak man looks for an excuse.

examples.text: Мы нашли простой способ решить задачу.
examples.trans: We found a simple way to solve the problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They just fired me.

examples.text: По контракту только я могу увольнять.
examples.trans: Under the contract, only I can fire cooks.

examples.text: Дима, я тебя только очень прошу.
examples.trans: Dima, I only ask you very much.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, и к Кате поближе.
examples.trans: Very good, and closer to Katya.
Did another husband run away from you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.
Alright, bye, have a safe trip!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Катя сегодня уезжает в другой город.
examples.trans: Katya is leaving for another city today.
Thank goodness, we dodged a bullet today!

examples.text: Давай сегодня спокойно, я тебя умоляю.
examples.trans: Let's keep it calm today, I beg you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Calm down, my husband hired you.

examples.text: Давай сегодня спокойно, я тебя умоляю.
examples.trans: Let's keep it calm today, I beg you.
You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'молять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I beg', paired with 'умолить'.

examples.text: Давай сегодня спокойно, я тебя умоляю.
examples.trans: Let's keep it calm today, I beg you.
I'm begging you, help!
He's begging the governor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to feed', paired with 'накормить'.

examples.trans: The cook feeds the guests a delicious lunch.

examples.text: Быстро беги на кухню и корми людей!
examples.trans: Quickly run to the kitchen and feed people!

examples.text: Ты кормишь рыбу лучше наших гостей.
examples.trans: You feed the fish better than our guests.

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Только у вас кормят намного лучше.
examples.trans: Only they feed people much better at your place.
In prison it will be much worse.
Today is much warmer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Victor Petrovich, what happened?

examples.text: А ещё лучше — из этого города.
examples.trans: And even better, from this city.

examples.text: Только у вас кормят намного лучше.
examples.trans: Only they feed people much better at your place.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('rare, scarce, unusual').

examples.trans: These are rare animals for the evening.

examples.text: У меня есть много редких материалов.
examples.trans: I have many rare materials.

examples.text: Макс, почему редкие трюфели оказались на помойке?
examples.trans: Max, why did rare truffles end up in the dumpster?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'animals' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: These are rare animals for the evening.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

examples.text: Мне на вечере нужны милые животные.
examples.trans: I need cute animals at the evening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: These are rare animals for the evening.
We were collecting money for them.

examples.text: Чтобы вкусно её для вас приготовить.
examples.trans: In order to cook it deliciously for you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'in the evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: These are rare animals for the evening.
We are having a charity evening today.

examples.text: Я проведу этот вечер просто блестяще!
examples.trans: I will host this evening simply brilliantly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just call and tell him.

examples.text: Она выгонит нас, чтобы вас унизить.
examples.trans: She will kick us out to humiliate you.
They will be present at the event.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: Я очень хочу быть с Катей.
examples.trans: I really want to be with Katya.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'сутствовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be present / attend'.

related.gloss: not to to be present (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: They will be present at the event.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и присутствовать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to be present on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Yes, I already know that.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'at the event' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Tomorrow we have an important event.
They will be present at the event.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, there you go, it has started already.
These are rare animals for the evening.
Right here is our fur seal.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.
Our head cook there got sick.

examples.text: Нам нужно решить нашу деликатную проблему.
examples.trans: We need to solve our delicate problem.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sea / marine').

examples.trans: Right here is our fur seal.
And where is our fur seal?

examples.text: Сегодня у нас морской котик и норка.
examples.trans: Today we have a fur seal and a mink.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'fur seal / little cat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right here is our fur seal.
It is a dish that is served cold.
And where is our fur seal?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I still have to inspect the whole hotel.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы не сможете купить меня за деньги!
examples.trans: You cannot buy me with money!
Did you change your mind and come for the money?

examples.text: Нет, мне ваши деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: No, I do not need your money.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: I will go, bite each other without me.
No, I am going back to work.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'rescue / saving' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть спасение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always rescue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Excuse me, I need to go.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!
Mom, please stop him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, и к Кате поближе.
examples.trans: Very good, and closer to Katya.

examples.text: Тебя вспомнишь — и уже не так плохо.
examples.trans: One remembers you, and things do not seem so bad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I just did not try hard enough yesterday.

examples.text: Ну я же не вчера родился, а?
examples.trans: Well, I was not born yesterday, huh?
Yesterday I was at home.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'was born', paired with 'рождаться'.

examples.trans: I was born in Sineozersk.
Where were you born?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы договорились: ты не вмешиваешься в мою жизнь.
examples.trans: We agreed: you do not interfere in my life.

examples.text: Мы же пришли сюда за вами!
examples.trans: We came here following you, after all!

examples.text: А то, что мы с вами переспали...
examples.trans: And the fact that you and I slept together...

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('charity').

examples.trans: We are having a charity evening today.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень благотворительный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very charity choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'collected', paired with 'собрать'.

examples.trans: We were collecting money for them.
Gather the money!
We are collecting signatures.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Vitya, meet her right now.
Tell me straight: what do you want?

examples.text: А живую змею в кастрюлю спрятал.
examples.trans: And I hid the live snake in a pot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вспомнили, что у вас есть дочь?
examples.trans: Did you remember that you have a daughter?

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.
Victor Petrovich, what happened?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: За что она хотела меня уволить?
examples.trans: Why did she want to fire me?
They wanted to put me to sleep too!
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'вести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will spend', paired with 'проводить'.

examples.trans: I'll have a good time.
We spent the evening at home.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!
Just call and tell him.
I just did not try hard enough yesterday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'brilliantly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я проведу этот вечер просто блестяще!
examples.trans: I will host this evening simply brilliantly!

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно блестяще и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite brilliantly and calmly.
